tier_reason: README Performance section gives first-party speedups (~5.4x/~4-5x AVX-512 over own scalar; scalar at parity with tiny-keccak; keccak-asm ~1.3x over scalar; 8-wide ~5.5x over keccak-asm) measured on an unnamed 'Zen-class AVX-512 part'; no exact CPU model, and the public harness (examples/perf.rs, benches/keccak.rs) does not include the tiny-keccak/keccak-asm comparisons, so it cannot be A.

corrections.caveats: Young, single-organization (nxm-rs), 1-star project: repo created 2026-07-02 (not 2026-09-24), crate 0.1.0 published on crates.io 2026-07-02 (~3.2k downloads) though the README still calls it pre-release. Benchmark hardware is only 'a Zen-class AVX-512 part' (no exact CPU model). The external-baseline comparisons (tiny-keccak, keccak-asm) are README prose only: the public examples/perf.rs and benches/keccak.rs measure only the crate's own scalar vs batched paths, and keccak-asm is not even a dev-dependency. Batch speedup applies only to many equal-length independent inputs; single-message hashing is scalar. Legacy Keccak-256 (0x01 padding), not FIPS-202 SHA3. AGPL-3.0-or-later copyleft.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 1 star; crates.io keccak-batch 0.1.0 (~3.2k downloads); used as the batched hash in nxm-rs/nectar (Swarm BMT)

notes: Numbers match README exactly. last_commit 2026-07-24 on main is correct (repo pushed_at 2026-09-24 reflects activity on side branches such as perf/absorb-fast-path). License AGPL-3.0 (Cargo.toml says AGPL-3.0-or-later) is OSI, so copyable holds.

tier_reason: No benchmark page exists. README, OVERVIEW.md and CHANGELOG.md have only qualitative claims ('fast', 'Optimized performance for SHA3-...'), and the perfsys tool (tools/perfsys, documented in doc/source/performance-test-tool-perfsys-cli-options.rst) measures only the library itself, with no published results or OpenSSL comparison.

corrections.baseline: OpenSSL SHA-2/SHA-3 (implied incumbent only; no published comparison against it)
corrections.stars_or_usage: 388 stars; formerly Intel IPP Cryptography (intel/ipp-crypto, which now redirects here); vendored as a git submodule in intel/QAT_Engine (crypto_mb multi-buffer backend)
corrections.caveats: No first-party or third-party benchmark numbers found (README, OVERVIEW.md, CHANGELOG.md, perfsys docs, QAT_Engine docs); 'fast' is unquantified. The repo ships a perfsys performance tool (ps_ippcp, ps_crypto_mb) but publishes no results. Not FIPS 140-3 certified: README_FIPS.md says it is 'FIPS-Compliant' (CAVP algorithm testing only), not CMVP-certified. OpenSSL is not a generic no-dispatch baseline; it also has runtime-dispatched SHA-NI/AVX2 paths. Kept as a single Tier-D entry because it is Intel's widely referenced crypto primitives library.

notes: Metadata all check out (Apache-2.0, not archived or forked, last commit 2026-09-25, default branch develop). Main fixes: 'FIPS 140-3 validated' is false per README_FIPS.md, and the baseline wording wrongly said OpenSSL has no CPU dispatch. Not rejected despite <1k stars because it is widely referenced (Intel QAT_Engine submodule, formerly IPP Crypto).
